data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: after
sections.question: after
sections.summary: following in time; later than something else

senses.definition: used to show that one event or action happens later than another
examples: She went to bed after she had finished all her homework.
He called his mother after he arrived at the hotel.

senses.definition: at a time later than; following in position or order
examples: She went to the gym after work.
He arrived after dinner and missed the food.

answers.answer: She went to bed after she had finished all her homework.
He bought three afters at the market for his children.
She cooked the after in a big pot for Sunday dinner.
They planted an after in the garden and watered it daily.

sections.title: although
sections.question: although
sections.summary: despite the fact that; even though

senses.definition: used to introduce a statement that makes the main statement surprising or unexpected
examples: Although it was raining, she decided to walk to the park.
She passed the exam although she had not studied very much.

answers.answer: Although it was raining, she decided to walk to the park.
He bought two althoughs at the supermarket on Saturday.
She cooked the although in a large pan for dinner.
They planted an although in the garden last spring.

senses.definition: used to introduce the reason for something
examples: She wore a warm coat because it was very cold outside.
He was tired because he had worked all day without a break.

answers.answer: She wore a warm coat because it was very cold outside.
He bought a because at the market and took it home.
She cooked the because in the oven for Sunday dinner.
They planted a because in the garden near the gate.

sections.title: buy
sections.question: buy
sections.summary: to get something by paying money for it

senses.definition: to get something by paying money for it
examples: She went to the market to buy some fruit and vegetables.
He bought a new jacket because the old one was too small.

answers.answer: She went to the market to buy some fruit and vegetables.
He wants to buy the sun because he needs more light.
She tried to buy Thursday because she needed more time.
They went to buy sleep at the pharmacy for the baby.

sections.title: drink
sections.question: drink
sections.summary: to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it

senses.definition: to take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it
examples: She drinks a large glass of water every morning when she wakes up.
He drank two cups of coffee before going to work.

senses.definition: an amount of liquid that you drink
examples: Would you like a drink of water?
She ordered a cold drink at the café.

answers.answer: She drinks a large glass of water every morning when she wakes up.
He drinks his bicycle to school every morning.
She drank the classroom before the lesson started.
They drink their homework every evening before bed.

sections.title: drive
sections.question: drive
sections.summary: to operate a vehicle and control its movement

senses.definition: to operate a vehicle and control its direction and speed
examples: He drives to work every day because his office is far from home.
She drives her children to school when it rains.

answers.answer: He drives to work every day because his office is far from home.
She drives her breakfast every morning before school.
He drives the music very loudly in the kitchen.
They drive their homework every evening after dinner.

sections.title: eat
sections.question: eat
sections.summary: to put food in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it

senses.definition: to put food into your mouth, chew it, and swallow it
examples: She eats a healthy breakfast before going to school every morning.
He ate a big bowl of soup for lunch.

answers.answer: She eats a healthy breakfast before going to school every morning.
He eats his car to school every day.
She eats very quickly to the market on Saturday.
They eat the weather outside in the garden.

sections.title: go
sections.question: go
sections.summary: to move from one place to another

senses.definition: to move or travel from one place to another
examples: She goes to the library every Thursday after school.
He went to the market to buy some vegetables.

answers.answer: She goes to the library every Thursday after school.
He goes his coffee before work every morning.
She went the letter to the post office on Friday.
They go the weather at the park every weekend.

sections.title: if
sections.question: if
sections.summary: on the condition that; used to talk about a possibility

senses.definition: used to talk about a condition or a possible situation, and what happens or might happen as a result
examples: She will bring an umbrella if it rains tomorrow.
He will call you if he is going to be late.

answers.answer: She will bring an umbrella if it rains tomorrow.
He bought three ifs at the supermarket last Saturday.
She cooked the if in the kitchen for dinner on Sunday.
They planted an if in the garden near the flowers.

sections.title: important
sections.question: important
sections.summary: having great value or significance; necessary

senses.definition: having great value, meaning, or effect; necessary to pay attention to
examples: It is important to eat well and exercise regularly to stay healthy.
She has an important meeting at work tomorrow morning.

answers.answer: It is important to eat well and exercise regularly to stay healthy.
He bought an important at the shopping mall on Saturday.
She drove her important to the office every morning.
They cooked the important and served it with vegetables.
